ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a circle, and there is a horizontal tangent line at the bottom of the circle. From the point of tangency, a slanted line is connected to another point on the circle, forming a chord. The arc corresponding to this chord in the figure is labeled 100°, and 160° is also labeled on the right side. What is required is ∠10, labeled between the tangent line and the chord. Then reason: ∠10 is the angle formed by the tangent line and the chord at the point of tangency. According to the tangent-chord theorem, the angle formed by a tangent line and a chord equals half the measure of the arc it intercepts. Therefore ∠10 = 100° ÷ 2 = 50°.
